name: Green Day
label: Lookout!
lede: Two Rodeo teenagers, a $675 first album, and a garage in the East Bay that turned into 75 million records worldwide.

eras.title: Two kids from Rodeo, one label with $4,000
eras.text: Billie Joe Armstrong and Mike Dirnt start Sweet Children as fifteen-year-olds in a Rodeo garage, then tie their fate to Larry Livermore's Lookout! Records and the all-ages 924 Gilman Street scene in Berkeley.

years.h: [[Billie Joe Armstrong|5d06fe54-485a-4a07-b506-5f6f719448cb]] and [[Mike Dirnt|f332a312-e95b-4413-b6cc-1762a5a6a083]] start a band at fifteen
years.p: They first called it Desecrated Youth, with bassist Sean Hughes and drummer Raj Punjabi, rehearsing in Punjabi's garage in Rodeo, California, before settling on Sweet Children.

years.h: First show: Rod's Hickory Pit, Vallejo
years.p: Sweet Children play their first live gig at a Vallejo restaurant and bar.

years.h: [[John Kiffmeyer|9eb48aba-297f-42f7-b0f9-73ecc0738ae1]] takes the drum stool, Dirnt moves to bass
years.p: Kiffmeyer, who goes by Al Sobrante, replaces Raj Punjabi. When Sean Hughes leaves, Dirnt switches from guitar to bass, and the trio lineup is set.

years.cap: Green Day during Rock am Ring at Nürburgring, Nürburg, Rheinland-Pfalz, Germa... · Wikimedia
years.h: Larry Livermore signs them to Lookout!
years.p: [[Larry Livermore|427f8569-3791-4887-976c-242bb49a573f]], who runs Lookout! Records with $4,000 saved from unemployment benefits, puts out the 1,000 Hours EP. The band renames itself Green Day, a Bay Area phrase for a day spent smoking weed, according to Livermore.
years.xp:
Livermore saw Sweet Children play and decided on the spot they were worth a record. The name change came just before release, to avoid confusion with another local band, Sweet Baby.

The scene around them was 924 Gilman Street, the volunteer-run all-ages club in Berkeley where Green Day cut their teeth.

eras.title: Tre arrives, Kerplunk explodes
eras.text: Two cheap records establish Green Day as the Lookout! band to beat. Kiffmeyer heads to college, Tré Cool steps in from The Lookouts, and the lineup that lasts is set.

years.h: 39/Smooth, recorded in two days for $675
years.p: Green Day's first album for Lookout! is cut in two days on a budget of $675, according to Louder.

years.h: [[Tré Cool|0dcee02c-5d2c-4f5c-9d60-d58a4df32d9e]] replaces Kiffmeyer, who leaves for Humboldt State
years.p: Kiffmeyer quits to attend Humboldt State University. Tré Cool, drummer of Livermore's own band [[The Lookouts|700cf581-cc8c-49c1-93e3-489bf1719255]], fills in and stays for good.
years.xp: Tré was already a fixture in the Lookout! orbit through The Lookouts, the band Livermore led. What began as a temporary fill-in became the permanent job.

years.h: 1,039/Smoothed Out Slappy Hours gathers the early records
years.p: Lookout! bundles 39/Smooth with the Slappy and Sweet Children EPs into one collection, the way most people first meet the early band.

years.h: Kerplunk: 10,000 sold on day one
years.p: Recorded at Art of Ears in San Francisco for a budget of $2,000, it becomes Lookout!'s biggest seller, with 50,000 copies out by year's end.
years.xp: Recording took place in two sessions, May and September 1991, with Tré Cool on drums for the first time. Larry Livermore later recalled hearing it and knowing life would never be the same for the label or the band. It was released in the UK in December 1991 and in the US on January 17, 1992.

eras.title: Selling out, the loudest way possible
eras.text: Major labels circle the band, Reprise signs them, and Gilman Street closes its doors to them. Dookie turns three chords and a garbage bag of clothes into a global hit.

years.h: Green Day leave Lookout! for Reprise Records
years.p: The move to a major label costs them their home scene: they play a final show at 924 Gilman Street under a fake name and are then barred from the club.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the last Gilman show to September 3, 1993, while Louder places the fake-name gig at Christmas 1993. Either way, the club's strictly anti-major-label stance meant the band was no longer welcome.

years.h: Dookie: recorded in three weeks, sells 20 million in the US
years.p: Wikipedia says the Reprise debut was recorded in three weeks; "Longview", "Basket Case" and "When I Come Around" all hit #1 on Modern Rock Tracks.

years.cap: Green Day at the House of Blues in 2015 · Wikimedia
years.h: Mud fight at Woodstock '94 knocks out Mike Dirnt's teeth
years.p: During a mud fight with the crowd, a security guard punches Dirnt in the mouth and knocks out his teeth, according to Wikipedia.
years.xp: The set became one of the best-known moments of the festival, and it was finally released on vinyl for Record Store Day 2019 as Woodstock 1994.

years.h: Boston riot at the Hatch Shell
years.p: A free show at Hatch Memorial Shell ends in chaos: about 100 people are injured and 45 arrested, according to Wikipedia.

eras.title: After the hit: darker, stranger, folkier
eras.text: Green Day answer Dookie with a nastier record, a wedding-slow ballad, and a folk-punk turn, while a side project stays secret for a decade.

years.h: Insomniac: faster, darker, double platinum
years.p: Wikipedia notes the follow-up sold three million US copies, despite being angrier than Dookie.

years.h: Nimrod adds an acoustic ballad to the punk
years.p: "Good Riddance (Time of Your Life)" wins an MTV Video Music Award for Best Alternative Video, on a record that also touches surf, ska and folk.

years.h: Warning goes gold, and Green Day play a free show for artists
years.p: Warning is the first Green Day album since Dookie not to reach triple platinum. In November they play a free show at San Francisco City Hall to protest artist evictions.

years.h: The Network: Green Day in costume, unconfirmed for a decade
years.p: Money Money 2020 appears on Adeline Records from a band in masks and aliases. Green Day did not officially confirm it was them until 2013.

eras.title: The rock opera that saved them
eras.text: After the stolen tapes of a finished album, Green Day start over and write American Idiot, a concept record that sends them to the top of the Billboard 200 and to a Broadway stage.

years.h: American Idiot gives Green Day their first #1 album
years.p: The rock opera debuts at #1 on the Billboard 200 and goes on to sell six million US copies.
years.xp: It came after the master tapes of an earlier album, Cigarettes and Valentines, were stolen, so the band started from scratch. The record won the 2005 Grammy for Best Rock Album, and "Boulevard of Broken Dreams" took Record of the Year the following year.

years.h: Green Day take back their Lookout! masters
years.p: They cite a continuing breach of contract over unpaid royalties. Wikipedia says the move led Lookout! to lay off six of nine staff, and the label closed in 2012.

years.h: Foxboro Hot Tubs: garage-rock alter egos play small Bay Area rooms
years.p: Under that name the trio release Stop Drop and Roll!!! and play small clubs.

years.h: American Idiot opens on Broadway
years.p: The stage musical, first staged at Berkeley Repertory Theatre in September 2009, earns three Tony nominations and wins two, for lighting and scenic design.

eras.title: Trilogy, Rock Hall, reset
eras.text: A three-album run, an induction, and a split with Reprise close out the decade.

years.h: ¡Uno!, ¡Dos! and ¡Tré! arrive within three months
years.p: The trilogy lands on September 21, November 9 and December 7, 2012, the first Green Day studio records to feature Jason White.

years.cap: Green Day's Billie Joe Armstrong and Jason Freese performing on July 28, 2009. · Wikimedia
years.h: Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, and a Kiffmeyer reunion
years.p: Fall Out Boy induct Green Day in their first year of eligibility. Days earlier, the band played as Sweet Children with John Kiffmeyer.

years.h: Revolution Radio debuts at #1, and Reprise deal ends
years.p: After this album the band parts from Reprise Records.

eras.title: Stadiums again
eras.text: Green Day return with festival slots, a new album, and a big stage.

years.h: Saviors is their fourteenth studio album
years.p: Released January 19, 2024 with a Saviors Tour alongside The Smashing Pumpkins, Rancid and The Linda Lindas.
play: The American Dream Is Killing Me

years.h: Green Day play the Super Bowl LX opening ceremony
years.p: Wikipedia lists the performance as part of their most recent run.
